newsitem.title: USA: Death row dog at large after jailbreak.
newsitem.headline: Death row dog at large after jailbreak.

text.p: In the crime annals of Aiken, South Carolina, Abraham's case is filed under shaggy dog stories.
Arrested after attacking a policeman in a drugs bust, he sat for two years on death row. An appeal failed but the night before he was due to be executed, he was sprung from his cell.
He's now the lam -- and the judge has ordered a stay of execution after a deluge of protests to the state governor.
Abraham is a pit bull dog.
"We even had his steak ready for his last meal," Jenifer Barnes, shelter manager for Aiken Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, told Reuters on Friday.
Abraham was nabbed in 1995 after a friend of his owner ordered him to attack a policeman during a marijuana bust.
Judge Charles Simons ruled him a dangerous animal who should be destroyed. He spent two years in custody at the SPCA while the appeal process was exhausted.
"The owners went throught three levels of court to get him back," Barnes said.
They failed and Abraham was due to be put down on Thursday. But overnight an unknowm person broke him out.
Local people have phoned Gov. David Beasley's office appealing for clemency and Simons has agreed to a new hearing.
Abraham, still a fugitive on Friday morning, has become a local folk hero.
"He's the talk of the town," Barnes said.
But is he a vicious hoodlum?
"In my opinion no. All the people at the shelter were very attached to him," she said.
"If he don't know you, he's still a dangerous dog," city animal control officer Jeff Wilson told the Augusta Chronicle.
"He still has the potential and ability to bite. I know what his teeth feel like."
